text:
# Ray Traversal Algorithms

Also called: Hierarchical Ray Traversal, Octree Ray Casting

## Overview
Ray Traversal Algorithms are a family of hierarchical methods used in volume rendering to efficiently determine which voxels a view ray intersects, thereby skipping empty space and reducing computational cost. Unlike [uniform grid](#920-uniform-grid.md) [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md), which samples every voxel along the ray, these methods traverse an octree or [sparse voxel octree (SVO)](#8749-sparse-voxel-octree-svo.md) structure to jump directly to occupied regions [S1, S6, unofficial]. They differ from their siblings by focusing on the traversal logic itself—specifically how to descend, ascend, and step through the tree—rather than the shading or [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) performed at the leaves.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of hierarchical descent and ascent. The traversal begins at the root of the octree and determines which of the eight children (octants) the ray intersects. This is typically done by comparing the ray's position relative to the center of the current node's bounding box [S1][S2, unofficial][S6, S8, unofficial].

1.  **Child Selection:** For a node with center $\mathbf{c}$ and half-extent $s$, the ray position $\mathbf{p}$ determines the child index $k \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$:
    $$
    k = 4 \cdot \mathbb{I}(p_x \ge c_x) + 2 \cdot \mathbb{I}(p_y \ge c_y) + 1 \cdot \mathbb{I}(p_z \ge c_z)
    $$
    where $\mathbb{I}(\cdot)$ is the indicator function [S1][S2, unofficial][S6, S8, unofficial].

2.  **[Empty Space Skipping](#1002-empty-space-skipping.md):** If the selected child is marked as empty (or uniform), the traversal skips the subtree. This is achieved by advancing the ray parameter $t$ to the exit of the current node or using neighbor pointers to jump to the next potentially occupied node [S1, S6, S8, unofficial][G].

3.  **Leaf Handling:** Upon reaching a leaf node, the method typically switches to a fixed-step traversal (like DDA) within the leaf's voxel grid to sample the volume data [S1, S6, S8, unofficial][G].

4.  **Backtracking:** Because octrees are sparse and irregular, traversal often requires backtracking to the parent node when a ray exits a subtree or encounters an empty branch. This is implemented using an explicit stack (on GPU) or recursion (on [CPU](#10688-naive-sdf-generation-cpu.md)) [S4, S6, S8, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Sparse Voxel Octree Ray Traversal](2451-sparse-voxel-octree-ray-traversal.md)
[Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) Ray Traversal](#2989-sparse-voxel-octree-ray-tracing.md) is a hierarchical raycasting technique that renders sparse voxel data by traversing an [octree structure](#2792-octree-based-structures.md) along ray paths to find occupied cells and their bounding boxes. It solves the problem of efficiently rendering large, complex voxel scenes by skipping empty space using axis-aligned [slab intersection](#776-ray-box-intersection.md) logic, avoiding the need to sample every voxel. Unlike standard rasterization which requires mesh generation and draw calls per chunk, SVO ray tracing renders the entire scene with a single draw call (e.g., a fullscreen triangle) and no vertex buffers. It provides an implicit Level of Detail (LOD) mechanism by controlling traversal depth based on viewer distance or fixed maximum depth.

### [SVO Ray Tracing](3451-svo-ray-tracing.md)
SVO Ray Tracing renders volumetric data stored in a Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) by traversing the [tree structure](#4139-tree-based-structures-octree-pointer-tree-sparse-voxel-dag.md) to sample only occupied regions, thereby skipping empty space. It differs from uniform grid ray marching by using hierarchical node pointers to jump over empty voxels, and from BVH-based approaches by operating directly on the octree structure without an intermediate [bounding volume hierarchy](#2808-domain-based-bvh-with-range-bounding-boxes.md). The implementation in the primary source converts the SVO into a BVH-like structure for efficient [ray intersection](#7624-ray-ray-intersection.md), executing a depth-first traversal to perform [volume compositing](#4646-reconstruction-and-compositing-techniques.md).

### [Ray-Occlusion Traversal in Octree](5121-ray-occlusion-traversal-in-octree.md)
[Ray-Occlusion Traversal in Octree](#5121-ray-occlusion-traversal-in-octree.md) is a hierarchical ray-intersection algorithm that traverses an octree structure to determine if a ray intersects any solid voxel or leaf node, primarily used for shadow ray computation and [early termination](#4675-early-termination.md) in volume rendering. It differs from its siblings by explicitly handling rays starting inside or outside the root bounding box via plane intersection logic and using a fixed-depth descent loop with explicit parent-boundary checks to manage traversal state, rather than relying solely on [neighbor-finding](#2198-neighbor-finding.md) or bottom-up approaches.

### [Boundary Cell-Based Ray Casting](11256-boundary-cell-based-ray-casting.md)
[Boundary Cell-Based Ray Casting](#11256-boundary-cell-based-ray-casting.md) (BC-RC) is a fast serial [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) algorithm that accelerates volume rendering by skipping empty space using boundary cells. It improves upon the [PARC](#2930-polygon-assisted-ray-casting.md) algorithm by using tiny grid cells for more accurate boundary estimation and employing fast incremental parallel projection to reduce projection overhead. Unlike PARC, which uses pre-calculated sub-volumes whose projection is expensive when small, BC-RC projects only cells containing the object boundary.

### [Optimized Ray Casting](11373-optimized-ray-casting.md)
[Optimized Ray Casting](#11373-optimized-ray-casting.md) is a hierarchical volume rendering technique that accelerates [image-order rendering](#16-image-order-rendering.md) by combining [octree-based empty space skipping](#1610-empty-space-skipping-with-octree.md) with adaptive ray [density and alpha](#3052-raw2alpha-density-to-alpha-conversion.md) cutoffs. Unlike standard ray casting which samples every voxel along the view ray, this method skips transparent regions using an octree structure and terminates rays early when sufficient opacity is accumulated, significantly reducing computational cost for sparse or semi-transparent datasets. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Sparse Voxel Octree Ray Traversal](2451-sparse-voxel-octree-ray-traversal.md) by emphasizing adaptive ray casting (sub-sampling in high-frequency areas) and specific hardware-optimized pipeline stages ([cut planes](#887-clipping-plane-for-volume-suppression.md), coarse-to-fine refinement) rather than just traversal efficiency.

### Single-Ray Traversal Strategy
The implementation does not use [SIMD](#2564-voxel-trilinear-interpolation-simd.md) or packet tracing. Coherent techniques (like frustum-based traversals) are avoided because highly-variant scenes and pixels covering multiple voxels cause unnecessary work and potential performance decreases compared to single-ray techniques [S1].

### Galileo System
A system using kd-tree space subdivision for ray tracing, parallelized on a CPU cluster system [S2, unofficial].

### Optimized Raytracing Kernel for Distance Fields
Perform an additional intersection test for every leaf voxel found in the hierarchy traversal using the raymarching algorithm [S3, unofficial]. If the ray does not intersect the distance field, continue ray traversal. Add a premature stop when the valid mask is set to zero (no children) to render the model from various levels of detail dynamically. If the premature intersection with the distance field fails, continue traversal [S3, unofficial].

### Dynamic LOD Traversal
Stops traversing the octree when the projected area of the next intersected child voxel is smaller than the projected area of the pixel on the screen, skipping ray-isosurface intersection tests [S3, unofficial]. Implement a version similar to [cone tracing](#5679-cone-tracing.md), approximating the radius of a cone around the ray. Exploit the fact that [finite difference normal](#876-sdf-normal-estimation-via-finite-differences.md) calculation can be evaluated at any point in the voxel. Voxelized normals are only rendered when the entire projected voxel area is smaller than the pixel to remove aliasing effects [S3, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of using hierarchical structures to accelerate ray tracing in volumetric data has evolved from early octree-based [isosurface rendering](#7669-isosurface-rendering.md) to modern Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) techniques. The foundational work on interactive isosurface ray tracing of large octree volumes by Wald et al. [S1] established the single-ray traversal strategy, noting that coherent techniques often fail on large, variant data. Parallel systems like Galileo [S2, unofficial] explored CPU cluster parallelization using kd-trees. More recent developments focus on GPU-accelerated SVO traversal [S6, unofficial] and dynamic Level-of-Detail (LOD) strategies to balance quality and performance [S3, unofficial].
